clue.text: I got into bed, able to see only one side?

definitions.text: able to see only one side?

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it is placed inside it, here the pronoun and verb inside the sleeping place

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into bed, apparently lying so they can only see one side of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sleepy scene; the whole phrase 'I got into bed' is the wordplay, spelt out literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A prejudiced person sees only their own side of any question, which the question mark flags as playful.

clue.text: Poet is on fire

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., the national poet of Scotland
something alight is ablaze, giving the verb form for third person

explanation.surface: A poet whose passion is aflame.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is the Scottish poet; separately, something ablaze is said to be giving off flames in the present tense.

clue.text: Sailor seeming to upset this supreme commander

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and into disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor appears to be annoying the top military chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'upset' looks like the verb of the sentence but signals the rearrangement of all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is given to a commander-in-chief ranking above all other generals, a supreme military leader.

clue.text: Forest region in Alberta, I gather

indicators.note: region in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wooded area in the Canadian province of Alberta, so I understand.
explanation.definitionFit: The subarctic coniferous woodland of Canada and Siberia is a type of boreal forest.

clue.text: Aussie's excavating equipment

definitions.meaning: an Australian is informally called a ..., from goldfield and wartime slang; the 's stands for is
a machine that scoops out earth

explanation.surface: An Australian's tools for digging.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for an Australian soldier, and also names a mechanical excavator.

clue.text: Postpone using force to spear ruminants

indicators.note: to spear is to pierce, so the force letter goes right through the middle of the animals

parts.note: deer chew the cud, so are ruminants
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A hunter delays using strength to lance some grazing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something off until later is a direct synonym of delaying it.

clue.text: Inactive lecturer takes time to tour Sandhurst

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it, so the first pieces surround the academy

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
RMA, the Royal Military Academy, is at Sandhurst
T is the abbreviation for time, which the lecturer takes on after him

explanation.surface: An idle academic finds time to visit the army officer college.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer training academy, known by its initials RMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying asleep or unused, like a volcano, is not active; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Referendum mob riots: I am in it from the start

definitions.text: I am in it from the start

indicators.note: a mob that riots runs wild, so the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A crowd turns violent after a referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riots' looks like the verb of the sentence but is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An original member of a club or society has belonged to it since its beginning, as the speaker says.

clue.text: To arrest duke, back my revolutionary troops

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the rear piece holds the duke inside it

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: An order to back a plan to arrest a duke, given to a band of rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is part of the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet army grew from the Bolshevik forces of the 1917 Revolution, hence revolutionary soldiers.

clue.text: Easily outclass, circling?

definitions.meaning: to be far better than a rival without effort
literally, going round and round in circles

explanation.surface: Beating someone easily by going round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to beat someone with ease; read literally it describes running in loops around them.

clue.text: Outward appearance of champion Internet browser?

definitions.meaning: the exterior or visible face of something
an expert at surfing the web would be a ...

explanation.surface: How a top web user looks to others.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer or superficial look of something is its exterior face; split, the word is a surfing expert.

clue.text: Tree appears more bare, first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the comparative adjective

parts.note: balder means having less hair, so more bare

explanation.surface: A tree looks barer once its first leaves have dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Accidentally wet a prominent display

definitions.meaning: to spatter someone with water by mistake
a big showy feature, as in a front-page story

explanation.surface: Getting soaked by accident makes quite a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to spatter with liquid; the noun means a sensational showing, as in making a big impression.

clue.text: Cathedral put lass off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church that discouraged a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The great domed church in the City of London designed by Christopher Wren.

clue.text: Royal Engineer eats new fish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the new letter goes into the soldier

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An army engineer dines on a freshly caught fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper and its relatives are food fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Maiden interrupts tale involving violent emotion

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of something, so the letter sits within the narrative

parts.note: a story is a tale
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman breaks into a passionate story.
explanation.definitionFit: A relationship full of anger and quarrels is described as tempestuous, like turbulent weather.

clue.text: I come down around noon away from the sea

indicators.note: the first two pieces sit around the letter for midday

parts.note: to land is to come down

explanation.surface: A pilot reports touching down at midday, somewhere far from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior of a country lies away from its coastline.

clue.text: Parent's thanks for Italian food

parts.note: pa is a parent, with the possessive s
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A father thanks someone for his spaghetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and the like are the staple foods of Italy.

clue.text: Live in comfortable home, extremely close

indicators.note: the verb goes inside the cosy home

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
to live is to be, so are

explanation.surface: Settling in a cosy house, right nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near means closest of all, i.e. at the least distance.

clue.text: A second man succeeded in sporting contest

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A runner-up won a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket Test series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket series between England and Australia is a famous sporting competition.

clue.text: You must accept mark for subject

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the old pronoun holds the letter

parts.note: thee is the old form of you
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a grade for their topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a talk or piece of writing is its subject.

clue.text: Blameless, lacking strength to eat one medium fruit

indicators.note: eating puts food inside, so the following pieces go inside the word for lacking strength

parts.note: unable means lacking the power to do something
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: An innocent person too weak to eat a moderate-sized piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct beyond reproach cannot be challenged or faulted; synonym of faultless.

clue.text: Small, deficient track

parts.note: poor means lacking or inadequate

explanation.surface: A faint, inadequate trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The trail or droppings left by an animal, which hunters follow.

clue.text: Merit death upfront? Horribly severe

indicators.note: up front means at the start, so the first letter of death
horribly signals the letters being mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Does someone earn execution up front? That is cruelly harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'death' looks like part of the definition, but only its opening letter is used; 'Horribly' is the anagram signal on the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be worthy of something, to earn it, is to merit it; a verb synonym.
